13-slos.file: Developing a Google SRE Culture/13-SLOs and error budgets.md
facts: error budget = the unreliability/downtime you are willing to tolerate
100% reliability is the wrong target (slows feature releases)
while error budget remains / uptime above target, you can release features
budget can be spent on planned downtime, risky experiments, hardware/network failures
SLO = numerical reliability target agreed by stakeholders
SLOs are set just short of 100% (99.9%, three nines)
SLI formula: good events / valid events x 100%
SLIs map to user expectations: latency, correctness, freshness, throughput
SLO is the target for SLIs aggregated over time
SLA = promise to customers with a consequence (e.g. refund) if SLOs are missed
measure reliability as good interactions/total interactions, not good time/total time
being well within SLO = can move faster; SLOs show how fast is too fast
SLOs + error budgets create shared responsibility between dev and ops (break silos)

14-vision.file: Developing a Google SRE Culture/14-Share vision and knowledge.md
facts: three focus areas: unified vision, collaboration/communication, knowledge sharing
team vision = values, purpose, mission, strategy, goals
core values build trust and psychological safety
teams with purpose: higher satisfaction, less conflict
OKRs = Objectives and Key Results, used for very ambitious goals
service-oriented meetings: weekly, 30-60 min, designated lead, compulsory
meeting agenda: production changes, metrics, outages, paging events, action items
SRE team roles: tech lead, manager, project manager
collaborate with product development early in design, before code is committed
cross-training: hire for it; reduces cost/turnover, improves morale/productivity
g2g employee-to-employee network runs 80% of trainings
job shadowing as a knowledge-sharing practice
postmortems foster knowledge sharing; tools with real-time collaboration, open commenting, email notifications

18-cicd.file: Developing a Google SRE Culture/18-Continuous integration, continuous delivery, and canarying.md
facts: developers favor moonshots; SREs favor gradual change
change is best small and frequent, rolled out in small waves
CI = building, integrating, testing code in dev environment, more often -> quality
CD = can deploy to production frequently but may choose not to
SDLC stages: code, build, integrate, test, release, deploy, operate; CI/CD fills the middle
CI/CD benefits: less human error, higher quality, easier recovery, shorter time to market
canary in a coal mine metaphor: small expendable thing detects danger
canarying = deploy change to a small group of users, evaluate impact, then decide
requirement: canary population representative of the control population
requirement: only difference between canary and control is the change under test
requirement: canary small enough not to endanger overall service quality
requirement: simple, low cognitive load, easy to cancel
the canary requirements partly conflict with each other
canary bugs cost far less than a full rollout and can be reversed quickly

19-design.file: Developing a Google SRE Culture/19-Design thinking and prototyping.md
facts: lowering the cost of failure (CI/CD, canarying) enables innovation
design thinking = creativity + structure for complex problems
five phases: empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test
empathize: observe users, set aside own assumptions
define the problem from the user's point of view
ideate: generate many ideas, think outside the box
prototype: get ideas into the real world, experimental, before committing
test prototypes in a real-world setting with intended users
software mindset: focus on user, 10x thinking, then prototype
test gradually with CI/CD and canarying
prototype-driven culture: more ideas tested, faster failures, more successes
no right way to prototype: lego/physical, paper, clickable, role play, video
make prototypes real enough; more concrete -> more actionable feedback

23-vpc.file: Google Cloud Fundamentals_ Core Infrastructure/23-Connecting networks to Google VPC.md
facts: Cloud VPN: tunnel over the internet to connect VPC to other networks
Cloud Router + BGP exchange routes dynamically; new subnets propagate automatically
Direct Peering: router in same public data center as a Google point of presence
Carrier Peering: via a service-provider partner when not in a point of presence
peering is not covered by a Google SLA
Dedicated Interconnect: private direct connection to Google; SLA up to 99.99% with qualifying topology
Dedicated Interconnect can be backed up by a VPN
Partner Interconnect: through a supported provider; for sites that can't reach a colocation facility or don't need 10 Gbps
Partner Interconnect: Google not responsible for the third-party provider part
Cross-Cloud Interconnect: dedicated connectivity between Google Cloud and another cloud provider (multicloud)
choice depends on three questions: private addressing, bandwidth/performance, willing to install equipment in a PoP
private-to-private with OK internet connection -> Cloud VPN; no private need -> public IPs
private high-performance without installing equipment -> Partner Interconnect
can.t|isn.t an option|not an option|without install|no equipment|instead|cannot|unable|not (possible|feasible)
